test: North Carolina DMV Knowledge and Traffic Signs Tests (Class C)
edition: Based on the North Carolina Driver Handbook (text revised May 2025, print run 09/25; online PDF last updated September 2026) and 19A NCAC 03B .0201, checked October 2026

exam.rules: First-time North Carolina Class C applicants take the tests in person at an NCDMV driver license office. Two written tests are scored separately and each must be passed: a computer-based knowledge test on traffic laws and safe driving (80% required by rule; it is commonly reported as 25 questions with 20 correct needed), and a road signs test in which you identify 12 signs by color and shape and explain their meaning (9 of 12 correct required). Teens 15-17 take the knowledge, signs and vision tests for a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit after finishing driver education (30 classroom hours and 6 behind-the-wheel hours); adults 18+ may take them for a learner permit or go on to the vision and road tests for a license. Transfers from other states and renewals usually take only the signs and vision tests. Audio tests are available on request, and if you fail a knowledge or driving test for a regular Class C license you may retake it after seven calendar days.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit in North Carolina?
questions.explain: Teens at least 15 but under 18 who have completed approved driver education may apply for a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: Before testing for a learner permit, a North Carolina applicant under 18 must show completion of an approved driver education course that includes:
options: At least 30 hours of classroom instruction and 10 hours behind the wheel
At least 30 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours behind the wheel
At least 20 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours behind the wheel
At least 40 hours of classroom instruction only
questions.explain: Applicants under 18 must present a certificate for a course of at least 30 classroom hours and 6 behind-the-wheel hours.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: During the first six months of a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit, when may the permit holder drive?
options: At any hour, as long as the supervising driver is present
Between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m., alone or supervised
Between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m., with the supervising driver
Between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m., with the supervising driver
questions.explain: For the first six months, Level 1 driving is limited to 5 a.m.-9 p.m. and always with the supervising driver.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: After a Level 1 permit has been held for six months, the permit holder may:
options: Drive at any time, but only with a supervising driver
Drive alone between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.
Carry one passenger under 21 without supervision
questions.explain: Six months after issuance, a Level 1 holder may drive at any hour, but supervision is still always required.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: How long must a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit be held before applying for a Level 2 Limited Provisional License?
questions.explain: The Level 1 permit must be held for nine months before applying for Level 2.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: The driving log a Level 1 permit holder submits must show at least how much supervised driving?
options: 40 hours, including at least 8 hours at night
60 hours, including at least 10 hours at night
50 hours, including at least 10 hours at night
60 hours, including at least 20 hours at night
questions.explain: The log must document a minimum of 60 hours, with at least 10 of them at night, signed by the supervising driver.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: Who may ride in the front seat while a Level 1 permit holder is driving?
options: Any passenger wearing a seat belt
A sibling, if the supervising driver is in the back
questions.explain: With a Level 1 permit, no one except the driver and the supervising driver may be in the front seat.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Limited Learner Permit'

questions.q: A supervising driver for a North Carolina teen permit or Level 2 license must have held a driver license for at least:
questions.explain: The supervising driver must hold a valid license and must have been licensed for at least five years.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Supervising Driver'

questions.q: Who may act as the supervising driver for a Level 1 permit holder?
options: A parent, grandparent or guardian, or a responsible person the parent or guardian approves, licensed at least five years
Any adult passenger age 21 or older, licensed or not
Any licensed driver who is 18 or older
questions.explain: The supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent, guardian or approved responsible person who has been licensed at least five years.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing - Supervising Driver'

questions.q: To move up from Level 1 to Level 2 (or Level 2 to Level 3), a teen must have no convictions for moving violations, seat belt or cell phone infractions in the preceding:
questions.explain: Each upgrade requires a clean record of moving, seat belt and cell phone convictions for the previous six months.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing'

questions.q: What is the minimum age for a Level 2 Limited Provisional License?
questions.explain: Level 2 drivers must be at least 16 but under 18.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Level Two Limited Provisional License'

questions.q: A Level 2 Limited Provisional License holder may drive without supervision:
options: At any time of day or night
From 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., and at other times only when driving directly to or from work or a volunteer fire, rescue or EMS duty
questions.explain: Unsupervised Level 2 driving is allowed 5 a.m.-9 p.m., plus direct trips to or from work or volunteer emergency service.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Level Two Limited Provisional License'

questions.q: How long must a Level 2 Limited Provisional License be held before upgrading to a Level 3 Full Provisional License?
questions.explain: Level 2 must be held at least six months before applying for a Full Provisional License.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Level Two Limited Provisional License'

questions.q: When driving without supervision, a Level 2 driver may generally carry how many passengers under 21 who are not members of the driver's household?
options: One (with a limited exception for one more student being driven directly to or from school)
questions.explain: Only one non-household passenger under 21 is allowed, plus one additional student only when going directly to or from school.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Level Two Limited Provisional License'

questions.q: Which restriction still applies to a Level 3 Full Provisional License holder who is under 18?
options: No more than one passenger under 21
No use of a cell phone while driving, except for listed emergency calls
A supervising driver must be in the car
questions.explain: Level 3 removes time, supervision and passenger limits, but drivers under 18 still may not use a cell phone except for emergency calls.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Level Three Full Provisional License'

questions.q: In North Carolina, a regular (non-graduated) learner permit is available to people who are:
questions.explain: Regular learner permits are for persons 18 and older; younger applicants use the graduated licensing system.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Learner Permit'

questions.q: A person age 18 or older with a learner permit may drive only when:
options: Any licensed driver is somewhere in the vehicle
Driving on roads posted 45 mph or less
A person licensed to drive that vehicle is seated beside them
questions.explain: The permit holder must be accompanied by someone licensed for that vehicle who sits beside them.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Learner Permit'

questions.q: Which tests are required for a learner permit in North Carolina?
options: Vision and the road test only
Vision, traffic signs and the knowledge test
questions.explain: Learner permit testing covers vision, traffic signs and knowledge of motor vehicle laws; the road test is not required for a permit.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Learner Permit; Test Requirements for an Original Driver License'

questions.q: To pass the North Carolina traffic signs test, an applicant must:
options: Identify signs by their color and shape and explain what each means
Name the federal code number of each sign
Only read the words printed on each sign
questions.explain: The signs test requires identifying signs by color and shape and explaining their meaning.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Test Requirements - Traffic Signs'

questions.q: If you fail the knowledge test for a regular Class C license, how soon may you retake it?
questions.explain: NCDMV allows a failed knowledge or driving test for a regular Class C license to be retaken in seven calendar days.
questions.ref: NCDMV, 'Driver License Tests' web page (ncdot.gov/dmv), retest rule

questions.q: A new resident of North Carolina must obtain a North Carolina driver license within how many days of establishing residence?
questions.explain: New residents have 60 days to get a North Carolina license (30 days to transfer a CDL).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Moving to North Carolina'

questions.q: If your address changes, you must notify NCDMV and get a duplicate license within:
questions.explain: An address or name change must be reported within 60 days, and a duplicate license obtained.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Address Changes'

questions.q: A North Carolina driver license issued to a driver aged 18 through 65 is valid for:
questions.explain: Licenses issued at ages 18-65 last eight years; those issued at 66 or older last five years.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Duration and Renewal of License'

questions.q: For auto policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025, what are North Carolina's minimum liability insurance amounts?
options: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash, $25,000 property damage
$50,000 per person, $100,000 per crash, $25,000 property damage
$50,000 per person injured, $100,000 per crash for injuries, $50,000 property damage
$100,000 per person, $300,000 per crash, $100,000 property damage
questions.explain: Since July 1, 2025, North Carolina requires at least 50/100/50 liability coverage (the May 2025 handbook text still lists the older 30/60/25 minimums).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 7 How DMV Serves You, 'Insurance and Financial Responsibility'; NCDMV 'Insurance Requirements' web page (policies issued or renewed after July 1, 2025)

questions.q: For a driver 21 or older in a regular passenger vehicle, North Carolina's per se blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit is:
questions.explain: DWI can be proven by a BAC of 0.08 or more for non-commercial drivers.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Driving While Impaired'

questions.q: What BAC is enough to prove impaired driving for someone operating a commercial motor vehicle?
questions.explain: For commercial motor vehicle drivers the limit is 0.04.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Driving While Impaired'

questions.q: A driver under 21 who is convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body faces:
questions.explain: Under-21 drivers convicted of driving after consuming any alcohol or drugs lose their license for one year.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Alcohol and the Young Driver'

questions.q: For a provisional licensee (under 18), how much alcohol may be in their body while driving?
questions.explain: It is unlawful for a provisional licensee to drive after consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs; conviction brings a one-year revocation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'The Provisional Licensee'

questions.q: A driver charged with DWI willfully refuses a required chemical test. What happens to their license?
options: Immediate revocation for at least 30 days, plus a separate revocation of at least 12 months by DMV
Nothing, unless the driver is later convicted
questions.explain: Refusal brings an immediate civil revocation of at least 30 days and an additional DMV revocation of at least 12 months.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Driving While Impaired'

questions.q: If a chemical test shows a non-commercial driver's BAC is 0.08 or higher, the driving privilege is:
options: Revoked immediately for at least 30 days
questions.explain: A BAC of 0.08 or more (0.04 in a commercial vehicle) results in an immediate revocation of at least 30 days.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Driving While Impaired'

questions.q: Can a driver be convicted of DWI in North Carolina with a BAC below 0.08?
options: No, 0.08 is required for any DWI conviction
Yes, if their physical or mental faculties are shown to be appreciably impaired
questions.explain: DWI may be proven either by appreciable impairment from alcohol or drugs, or by a BAC at or above the legal limit.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Driving While Impaired'

questions.q: What is the license revocation for a first DWI conviction in North Carolina?
questions.explain: A first DWI conviction brings a mandatory one-year revocation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'If you are convicted of DWI'

questions.q: A second DWI conviction, where the prior offense occurred within three years, results in a revocation of:
questions.explain: A second conviction with a prior offense within three years carries a mandatory four-year revocation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'If you are convicted of DWI'

questions.q: A third DWI conviction, when at least one prior conviction occurred within the past five years, results in:
questions.explain: A third conviction with a prior within five years brings mandatory permanent revocation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'If you are convicted of DWI'

questions.q: A DWI conviction with a BAC of 0.15 or more will require:
options: An ignition interlock device on the vehicle
Daytime-only driving with no other conditions
questions.explain: A DWI with a BAC of 0.15 or higher (or another conviction within seven years) requires an ignition interlock.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration Restrictions'

questions.q: When a license is restored for the first time after a DWI revocation, the driver's alcohol concentration restriction is:
questions.explain: The first restoration carries a 0.04 restriction; a second or later restoration carries 0.00.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration Restrictions'

questions.q: Under North Carolina DWI laws, transporting an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a car is:
options: Allowed if it is in the back seat
Allowed if the driver is not drinking
Allowed if it is beer or wine
questions.explain: DWI laws prohibit transporting an open container of any alcoholic beverage in the passenger area.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'DWI Laws'

questions.q: What is the only thing that sobers up a person who has been drinking?
questions.explain: Only time removes alcohol from the body; coffee, food and showers do not.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Driver Safety - Alcohol'

questions.q: Alcohol is a depressant. One of its effects on drivers is that it:
options: Sharpens judgment of speed and distance
Gives false confidence while slowing reactions
Has no effect if the driver feels fine
questions.explain: Alcohol slows brain function, reduces judgment of speed and distance, and gives false confidence.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Driver Safety - Alcohol'

questions.q: A person under 21 who is convicted of trying to buy alcohol with a fake ID faces:
questions.explain: Underage attempts to buy alcohol, including with a fraudulent ID, bring a one-year revocation on conviction.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Alcohol and the Young Driver'

questions.q: If you let someone under 21 use your driver license to try to buy alcohol and are convicted, your license will be:
questions.explain: Allowing your license or ID to be used by an underage person to buy alcohol carries a one-year revocation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'Alcohol and the Young Driver'

questions.q: Before driving privileges are reinstated after a DWI conviction, North Carolina requires the driver to:
questions.explain: Anyone convicted of DWI must get a substance abuse assessment before reinstatement.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 2 Alcohol and the Law, 'DWI Laws'

questions.q: At how many driver license points may a North Carolina driver be assigned to a driver improvement clinic?
questions.explain: Accumulating seven points may lead to assignment to a driver improvement clinic.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Driver License Points'

questions.q: Satisfactorily completing a driver improvement clinic removes how many points from your record?
questions.explain: Completing the clinic deducts three points.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Driver License Points'

questions.q: Your license may be suspended if you accumulate how many points within three years?
questions.explain: Accumulating 12 points within three years can result in suspension.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Driver License Points'

questions.q: After your license is reinstated from a points suspension, a second suspension can result from accumulating how many points within three years?
questions.explain: Eight points within three years after reinstatement can lead to a second suspension.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Driver License Points'

questions.q: How long is a first suspension under the point system?
questions.explain: A first point-system suspension may be for 60 days; the second 6 months; the third 12 months.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Driver License Points'

questions.q: How many driver license points are assessed for passing a stopped school bus in a passenger vehicle?
questions.explain: Passing a stopped school bus carries 5 points (8 in a commercial vehicle).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Points table'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for a following too closely conviction (non-commercial)?
questions.explain: Following too closely, reckless driving, illegal passing and driving on the wrong side of the road each carry 4 points.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Points table'

questions.q: How many points does running a red light or a stop sign add to a non-commercial driver's record?
questions.explain: Running through a stop sign or a red light carries 3 points.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Points table'

questions.q: Which of these convictions adds NO driver license points?
options: Failure to yield right of way
questions.explain: Illegal parking is one of the offenses for which no points are assessed.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Points - No points'

questions.q: Failing to properly restrain a child in a child restraint or seat belt adds how many points?
questions.explain: Failure to properly restrain a child carries 2 points.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Points table'

questions.q: If you are convicted of driving more than 15 mph over the limit while going faster than 55 mph, your license will be revoked for at least:
questions.explain: Speeding more than 15 mph over the limit at a speed above 55 mph brings a revocation of at least 30 days.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Suspensions'

questions.q: A provisional licensee (under 18) convicted of a second moving violation within 12 months may have the license suspended for:
questions.explain: Second moving violation in 12 months: 30 days; third: 90 days; fourth: six months.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Provisional Licensee (under age 18)'

questions.q: A provisional licensee convicted of a third moving violation within a 12-month period may be suspended for:
questions.explain: The third moving violation within 12 months brings a 90-day suspension for drivers under 18.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Provisional Licensee (under age 18)'

questions.q: When a driving privilege is reinstated after a points suspension, what happens to the driver license points?
options: They are canceled, but insurance points are not affected
They are converted to insurance points
They remain for three more years
questions.explain: Reinstatement cancels prior driver license points; insurance points are a separate system.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 3 Your Driving Privilege, 'Driver License Points'

questions.q: At an intersection with no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right of way?
options: The vehicle already in the intersection
questions.explain: A vehicle already in the intersection goes ahead of any vehicle that has not entered.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Special Driving Situations - right-of-way rules'

questions.q: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time from different roads. Who must yield?
options: The driver on the left yields to the vehicle on the right
The driver on the right yields to the vehicle on the left
questions.explain: When two vehicles arrive together, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Special Driving Situations - right-of-way rules'

questions.q: You want to turn left at an intersection and an oncoming car is going straight. Who has the right of way?
options: You, because left turns have priority at intersections
Whoever reached the intersection first, always
questions.explain: A driver turning left must signal and wait; the vehicle going straight has the right of way.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Right-of-Way at Intersections'

questions.q: When you come to a stop sign at a through street, you must:
options: Stop only if a vehicle is approaching from the left
Stop completely and yield to traffic on the through street
Slow down and go if no one is directly in front
questions.explain: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop and yield to through traffic before proceeding.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Right-of-Way at Intersections'

questions.q: When leaving a private driveway to enter a street, you must:
options: Yield only to vehicles on the left
Sound the horn and pull out
Stop and yield to all vehicles and pedestrians
questions.explain: Coming out of a private driveway, you must stop and let all vehicles and pedestrians go first.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Right-of-Way at Intersections'

questions.q: At an intersection without traffic signals, a pedestrian is crossing in an unmarked crosswalk. You must:
options: Honk so the pedestrian moves faster
Yield only if the pedestrian is a child
Proceed, since the crosswalk is not painted
questions.explain: At unsignaled intersections, pedestrians have the right of way in marked crosswalks and in unmarked crosswalks formed by extending the sidewalks.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'The Driver and Pedestrian'

questions.q: You are turning right on a green light and a pedestrian is crossing the street you are turning into, also with a green signal. Who has the right of way?
options: You, because right turns have priority
You, because you have a green light
questions.explain: Pedestrians crossing on green have the right of way over all vehicles, including those turning across their path.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'The Driver and Pedestrian'

questions.q: The signal turns red while a pedestrian is still in the street in front of you. You should:
options: Let the pedestrian finish crossing safely
Proceed once your light is green
Sound the horn and drive around them
questions.explain: If the signal changes while a pedestrian is still in the street, drivers must allow them to finish crossing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'The Driver and Pedestrian'

questions.q: At an intersection without traffic signals, a pedestrian is holding out a white cane or is using a guide dog. You should:
options: Honk to let the pedestrian know you are there
Stop and give the pedestrian the right of way
Proceed if the pedestrian is not yet in your lane
questions.explain: The law gives special consideration to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'The Driver and Pedestrian'

questions.q: If you fail to yield to a pedestrian when turning right on a red light, the penalty is:
options: A fine of not less than $100 and not more than $500
questions.explain: Failure to yield to a pedestrian while turning right on red carries a $100-$500 penalty.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: An ambulance using its siren and flashing lights is approaching from behind on a two-lane road. You must:
options: Pull to the left and slow down
Pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explain: Move to the right curb or road edge, come to a full stop and stay stopped until the emergency vehicle goes by.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergency and Law Enforcement Vehicles'

questions.q: You are on a four-lane limited-access highway with a median. An emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches in the opposite direction. You:
options: Are not required to pull over and stop
Must stop on the right shoulder
questions.explain: The yield requirement does not apply to vehicles traveling in the opposite direction on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergency and Law Enforcement Vehicles'

questions.q: On a highway with two or more lanes in your direction, you approach a police car stopped on the shoulder with its warning lights on. You must:
options: Sound your horn as you pass
Move into a lane not next to the stopped vehicle, if you can do so safely, and stay there until past it
questions.explain: North Carolina's move-over law requires moving to a lane not nearest the parked emergency or service vehicle.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergency and Law Enforcement Vehicles - Move Over'

questions.q: On a road with only one lane in your direction, you approach a tow truck helping a motorist on the shoulder with its warning lights flashing. You must:
options: Slow down and pass at a reduced, safe speed
Stop until the tow truck leaves
Cross the center line no matter what
questions.explain: With only one lane in your direction, the move-over law requires slowing to a reduced, safe speed until completely past.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergency and Law Enforcement Vehicles - Move Over'

questions.q: On a two-lane road, a school bus ahead stops and shows flashing red lights and its stop arm. Who must stop?
options: No one, if no children are visible
Only traffic coming toward the bus
questions.explain: On a two-lane roadway, all traffic from both directions must stop for a stopped school bus.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: On a four-lane road with no median, a school bus stops to load children. Who must stop?
options: Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
questions.explain: On a four-lane roadway without a median separation, traffic in both directions must stop.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, a school bus stops on the other side of the median. You are traveling in the opposite direction. You:
options: Must stop only if children are crossing
Must stop and wait for the bus to signal
questions.explain: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only traffic following the bus must stop.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: On a road of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, a stopped school bus with flashing red lights requires:
options: Traffic in both directions to stop
Only traffic following the bus to stop
questions.explain: On roads of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, only vehicles following the bus must stop.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: On a two-lane road with a center turning lane, a school bus stops for passengers. Who must stop?
options: Only drivers in the center turning lane
questions.explain: A two-lane road with a center turn lane is treated like a two-lane road: all traffic must stop.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: After stopping for a school bus, you may proceed when:
options: The children have reached the sidewalk
The stop arm is withdrawn, the red lights are off and the bus has started to move
The bus driver waves you on, even with lights flashing
questions.explain: Remain stopped until the mechanical stop signal is withdrawn, the flashing red lights are off and the bus begins moving.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: At a railroad crossing, which has the right of way?
options: The train, over all highway traffic including emergency vehicles
questions.explain: Trains always have the right of way, even over police, fire and ambulance vehicles.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad Crossing Safety'

questions.q: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: Vehicles and bicyclists already in the roundabout
No one; entering traffic has priority
Vehicles waiting to enter on your right
Only trucks using the truck apron
questions.explain: Drivers entering yield to vehicles and bicyclists already in the roundabout.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: A funeral procession is going through a red light at an intersection, and your light is green. You should:
options: Honk and move into the intersection
Not enter unless you can do so safely without crossing the procession's path
Proceed, because you have a green light
questions.explain: Drivers not in the procession may not enter the intersection, even on green, unless it can be done safely without crossing the procession's path.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Funeral Processions'

questions.q: You approach an intersection where the traffic lights are completely dark because of a power outage and no officer is directing traffic. You should:
options: Yield only to vehicles on the left
Treat it as an all-way stop
Proceed at normal speed if on the larger road
Treat it as a yield sign
questions.explain: A malfunctioning or dark signal is treated as though the intersection had stop signs on all approaches.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: Even when you have the right of way at an intersection, North Carolina law requires you to:
options: Speed up to clear it quickly
questions.explain: The law requires slowing at intersections even with the right of way.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Special Driving Situations'

questions.q: On a four-lane highway divided by a median more than 30 feet wide, each crossing of a roadway is treated as:
questions.explain: When a median is more than 30 feet wide, each crossing constitutes a separate intersection.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Special Driving Situations'

questions.q: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic light. You should:
options: Stop and wait for the light to turn green
Follow whichever is safer for you
Follow the officer's signals instead of the light
questions.explain: When an officer is directing traffic, obey the officer's hand signals instead of normal signals or signs.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Officers'

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching a roundabout you are about to enter. You should:
options: Not enter; if already inside, exit first and then pull over
Enter quickly and stop inside the roundabout
questions.explain: Never enter a roundabout while an emergency vehicle is passing through; if already in it, exit and then pull over.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts - Tips & Reminders'

questions.q: Unless another limit is posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a paved street with a center line inside North Carolina cities and towns?
questions.explain: Inside cities and towns the default limit is 35 mph unless a different limit is posted (from Dec. 1, 2026, unpaved roads and roads without a center line default to 25 mph).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed - Maximum Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a paved road with a center line outside North Carolina cities and towns?
questions.explain: Outside cities and towns the default maximum is 55 mph unless posted otherwise (from Dec. 1, 2026, unpaved roads and roads without a center line default to 25 mph).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed - Maximum Speed Limits'

questions.q: According to the handbook's table, the maximum speed limit for interstates in North Carolina is:
questions.explain: The maximum speed limit table lists 70 mph for interstates.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed - Maximum Speed Limits'

questions.q: What is the maximum speed limit for a school bus in North Carolina?
questions.explain: School buses are limited to 45 mph; school activity buses to 55 mph.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses; Maximum Speed Limits'

questions.q: North Carolina's recommended rule for a safe following distance in normal conditions is:
options: One car length for every 20 mph
questions.explain: Allow at least two seconds between the vehicle ahead passing a fixed point and your vehicle reaching it.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Following - The Two-Second Rule'

questions.q: How do you check that you are following at least two seconds behind?
options: Stay close enough to read its license plate
Keep two car lengths between you and the car ahead
Count two seconds after the car ahead brakes
When the car ahead passes a fixed point, count; you should not reach that point before two seconds pass
questions.explain: The two-second rule measures time between the vehicle ahead passing a point and you reaching the same point.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Following - The Two-Second Rule'

questions.q: Under ideal conditions, about how far does a car traveling 55 mph need to stop completely?
questions.explain: At 55 mph, a vehicle needs approximately 211 feet to stop in ideal conditions.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed to Driving Conditions'

questions.q: According to studies cited in the handbook, a vehicle moving well below the posted speed limit is:
options: More likely to cause or be involved in a crash than one moving at normal speed
Always the safest vehicle on the road
Never a hazard to other drivers
questions.explain: Vehicles moving considerably slower than traffic are more likely to be involved in crashes.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed to Driving Conditions'

questions.q: Which statement about speed limits is correct?
options: Speed limits apply only in daylight
You may exceed the limit by 5 mph when passing
Never drive faster than posted, and drive slower when conditions make the posted speed unsafe
The posted limit is always a safe speed
questions.explain: Never exceed the posted limit or a speed that is unreasonable for existing conditions.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed - most important rules about speed'

questions.q: As your speed increases, you should:
questions.explain: The faster you go, the farther ahead you must be able to see to stop in time.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed; Interstate Highways tips'

questions.q: Compared to dry pavement, how much slower should you drive on wet pavement?
options: Half the posted speed at all times
questions.explain: Drive at least five to 10 mph slower on wet pavement than on dry pavement.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hazardous Driving - Rain'

questions.q: In rain, what following distance should you allow?
options: At least twice the normal following distance
questions.explain: Stopping distances increase on slippery pavement, so allow at least twice the normal following distance.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hazardous Driving - Rain'

questions.q: On packed snow, the handbook recommends reducing your speed by:
options: Nothing, if you have snow tires
questions.explain: On packed snow, cut your speed by more than half; on ice, slow to a crawl.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Snow and Ice'

questions.q: When stopping on snowy or icy roads, allow at least how much stopping distance?
options: One and a half times the normal distance
questions.explain: Allow at least three times the normal stopping distance on snow or ice.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Snow and Ice'

questions.q: Modern roundabouts are designed for travel at about:
questions.explain: Modern roundabouts require lower speeds of about 15-20 mph.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: The best way to handle a curve is to:
options: Slow down before you enter the curve
Brake hard in the middle of the curve
questions.explain: Slow before entering so you don't need to brake in the curve, then accelerate gradually through it.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Rounding a Curve'

questions.q: When approaching a curve while traveling downhill, you should:
options: Keep your speed until the curve begins
Shift to a lower gear and begin braking earlier
questions.explain: Downhill curves call for a lower gear, earlier braking and a slower approach.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Rounding a Curve'

questions.q: You are driving slowly and a line of traffic has built up behind you on a two-lane road. You should:
options: Pull to the side of the road when safe and let them pass
Keep going; they can pass when legal
Brake to make them back off
questions.explain: If traffic collects behind you, pull over, stop and let vehicles pass.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting Your Speed to Driving Conditions'

questions.q: When entering an interstate, you should:
options: Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, then merge
Merge immediately at the start of the ramp
Enter slowly and let traffic go around you
questions.explain: Use the acceleration lane until your speed matches traffic, then merge safely.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Interstate Highways'

questions.q: When exiting an interstate, you should:
options: Signal well in advance and slow down only after moving into the deceleration lane
Brake hard just before the ramp
Slow down in the travel lane before the exit
Change lanes across all lanes at the last second
questions.explain: Signal early and enter the deceleration lane without slowing in traffic; then slow to the posted exit speed.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Interstate Highways'

questions.q: At night, you should never drive at a speed at which you:
options: Need to use your low beams
Cannot stop within the distance you can see ahead
questions.explain: Never outdrive your headlights: you must be able to stop within the distance you can see.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: When driving slower than the posted speed on a multi-lane highway, you should use:
options: The far right lane, except when passing, turning left or avoiding an obstruction
questions.explain: Slower drivers on multi-lane highways keep to the extreme right lane.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Driving on Your Side of the Road'

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should:
options: Stay close to the right edge so no vehicle can get between you and the curb
Swing wide to the left first
Turn from the center of the road
questions.explain: For right turns, stay close to the right edge, slow before the turn, then accelerate slightly.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Turning'

questions.q: How far before turning or stopping must you signal on a street with a speed limit under 45 mph?
questions.explain: Signal at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Flashing Turn Signals'

questions.q: If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, you should signal at least how far before turning?
questions.explain: At 45 mph or higher, signal at least the last 200 feet before the turn.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Flashing Turn Signals'

questions.q: To signal a left turn by hand, the driver extends the left arm:
questions.explain: A left-turn hand signal is the arm and hand held straight out.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hand Signals'

questions.q: To signal a right turn by hand, the driver holds the left arm:
options: Down with the palm facing back
Out with the forearm and hand pointing up
questions.explain: Right turn: arm straight out with forearm and hand straight up, palm forward.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hand Signals'

questions.q: A driver's left arm extended downward with the palm facing back means the driver is:
questions.explain: Pointing the arm and hand down, palm back, signals stopping or slowing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hand Signals'

questions.q: What is the correct order before changing lanes?
options: Check mirrors, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, signal, then move
questions.explain: Check mirrors and blind spot, signal in advance, then change lanes.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Changing Lanes'

questions.q: On a highway with three or more lanes, before moving into the next lane you should also check:
options: Nothing else if you have signaled
The shoulder to your right only
The lane beyond it, in case another driver is moving into the same space
questions.explain: Check the lane you're entering and the lane beyond so another vehicle isn't planning to move into the same space.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Changing Lanes'

questions.q: When you sound your horn before passing on a two-lane road, the driver ahead is legally obligated to:
options: Help you pass, by moving right and not speeding up
questions.explain: The horn signal places the driver being passed under a legal duty to help you pass.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Passing'

questions.q: When passing another vehicle, North Carolina law requires you to pass at least how far to its left?
questions.explain: State law requires a passing driver to leave at least two feet between their vehicle and the one being passed.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Passing'

questions.q: Passing is unsafe and usually illegal on a hill or curve where you cannot see at least how far ahead?
questions.explain: Do not pass on any curve or hill where you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Passing'

questions.q: Where is passing on the right allowed?
options: On a highway with at least two lanes in each direction
Whenever the driver ahead is slow
On any two-lane road if the shoulder is paved
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed on multi-lane highways, one-way streets, around a vehicle turning left, or in a right-turn lane.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Passing on the right'

questions.q: On a three-lane highway, you may pass only:
options: In the center lane, and only where it is marked for passing in your direction
questions.explain: On three-lane highways, pass only in the center lane where marked for your direction (unless the vehicle there is turning left).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Passing on the right'

questions.q: Another car is passing you and its driver sounds the horn. You should:
options: Move toward the right edge and not increase your speed
Speed up so it can't cut in
questions.explain: When being passed, help the other driver: move right and never speed up.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'When your vehicle is being passed'

questions.q: You have NOT passed safely if:
options: You returned when you could see the car in your mirror
The vehicle you passed had to slow down to let you back into your lane
questions.explain: A pass is unsafe if the passed vehicle must slow down to let you back in.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Passing'

questions.q: When backing up, you should:
options: Back quickly to limit time in traffic
Look over your right shoulder through the rear window and back slowly, no faster than 10 mph
Look through the side window only
questions.explain: Steer with the left hand, look over your right shoulder, and back slowly - not more than 10 mph.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Backing'

questions.q: In a single-lane roundabout, to make what would be a left turn at a normal intersection, you travel:
options: About three-quarters of the way around, then exit right
questions.explain: A quarter turn = right, halfway = straight, three-quarters = left, full circle = U-turn.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts - Single-Lane Roundabout'

questions.q: In a multi-lane roundabout, which lane is typically used to go straight, turn left or make a U-turn, according to the handbook?
options: Either lane, changing lanes inside as needed
questions.explain: Typically use the right lane to exit right and the left lane to go straight, turn left or U-turn; do not change lanes inside.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts - Multi-Lane Roundabout'

questions.q: While inside a multi-lane roundabout, you should:
options: Stop to let entering cars in
questions.explain: Choose your lane before entering and do not change lanes within the roundabout.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts - Multi-Lane Roundabout'

questions.q: In city traffic, you realize you are not in the proper lane for a turn at the next intersection. You should:
options: Turn from the wrong lane carefully
Stop in your lane until a gap appears
Continue to the next intersection and turn there
Cut across lanes at the last moment
questions.explain: If you are not in the proper lane, continue on and turn at the next intersection.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'City Driving'

questions.q: On a one-way street with several lanes, through traffic should generally use:
options: The center lane(s), leaving the outside lanes for turning
questions.explain: On one-way streets use center lanes for through travel and outside lanes for turning.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'City Driving'

questions.q: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?
options: Stop and wait for a gap to back up
Make a U-turn through the median
questions.explain: Never slow, back up or turn around after missing an exit; take the next exit.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Entering and Exiting the Interstate'

questions.q: On an interstate, which lane(s) should be used for passing?
options: The left lane(s); keep right otherwise
questions.explain: Keep to the right and use the left lanes for passing on interstates.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Interstate Highways'

questions.q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in North Carolina?
questions.explain: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of the entrance to a fire station?
questions.explain: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire station entrance.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: Where there is a curb, you may not park within how many feet of the curb line of an intersecting street?
questions.explain: No parking within 25 feet of the curb line of an intersecting street (15 feet from the right-of-way lines where there is no curb).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: Where there is no curb, you may not park within how many feet of the intersecting right-of-way lines?
questions.explain: Without a curb, the limit is 15 feet from the intersecting right-of-way lines.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: Parking on a highway shoulder is illegal unless your vehicle can be seen by approaching drivers from both directions for at least:
questions.explain: A vehicle on the shoulder must be visible from both directions for at least 200 feet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: Outside city limits, you may not park within how many feet of a fire or fire truck?
questions.explain: Inside city limits the rule is one block; outside cities it is 400 feet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of an emergency vehicle that has stopped to investigate a crash or give assistance?
questions.explain: Do not park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle stopped at a crash or to give help.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergency and Law Enforcement Vehicles'

questions.q: Before pulling out of a parallel parking space on the right side of the street, you should:
options: Sound your horn and pull out
Check for approaching traffic and signal left
questions.explain: Check traffic and give a left-turn signal before pulling out (unless parked on the left side of a one-way street).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking'

questions.q: Except on one-way streets, you should always park:
options: On the right side of the road
On the left side of the road
In the travel lane with flashers on
questions.explain: Park on the right-hand side of the road; only on one-way streets may you park on the left.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking'

questions.q: Parking within the right of way of an interstate highway is allowed:
options: Only in designated parking areas or in an emergency
questions.explain: Parking anywhere within the interstate right of way is prohibited except in designated areas or emergencies.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: Which of these is a place you must never park?
options: On a residential street 30 feet from an intersection
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited on crosswalks, sidewalks and bridges.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Parking - Places where you should not park'

questions.q: When you park on or along a highway at night, you should:
options: Leave your headlights on low beam
Turn on your emergency flashers and not leave your headlights on
questions.explain: Use emergency flashers when parked along a highway at night; headlights left on can blind oncoming drivers.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: To help prevent auto theft when you leave your vehicle, you should:
options: Hide the key under the floor mat
Leave the engine running for a quick stop
Never leave the key in the ignition
questions.explain: Never leave the key in the ignition of an unattended vehicle.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Auto Theft Prevention'

questions.q: Under North Carolina law, bicycles are:
options: Vehicles, and their riders must obey traffic laws, including DWI laws
questions.explain: Bicycles are vehicles; bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws, including DWI laws.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles'

questions.q: A bicyclist is riding in the middle of the travel lane ahead of you. You should understand that:
options: Bicycles are not allowed in travel lanes
You may pass within the same lane at any distance
Bicyclists may use the full lane when conditions require it
The bicyclist must ride on the shoulder
questions.explain: Motorists should expect bicyclists in the roadway; traffic conditions may require them to use the full lane.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles'

questions.q: The safest way to pass a bicyclist is to:
options: Squeeze past within the same lane
Follow closely until the road widens
Honk until the cyclist moves onto the shoulder
Change lanes, passing only when there is plenty of room and no oncoming traffic
questions.explain: Pass only with abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic; changing lanes is safest.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Pass with Care'

questions.q: At night, a bicycle in North Carolina must have a front light visible from at least:
questions.explain: The front light must be visible at least 300 feet; the rear red light or reflector at least 200 feet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Be Visible'

questions.q: Which bicycle riders and passengers must wear an approved helmet in North Carolina?
questions.explain: All bicycle riders and passengers under 16 must wear an approved protective helmet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Be Visible'

questions.q: When turning right across a bicycle lane at an intersection, the main danger is:
options: A crash with a bicyclist going straight on your right
Pedestrians on the far corner only
questions.explain: Because bicyclists ride to the right of motor traffic, right-turning drivers risk hitting a cyclist going straight.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Bicycle Lanes'

questions.q: How must you pass a motorcycle?
options: Share its lane if there is room
Pass within the same lane at 2 feet
Change lanes and pass as you would a larger vehicle
questions.explain: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of the lane.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: When passing a moped riding on the right side of the lane, you must stay at least:
options: 2 feet to the left of it
1 foot to the left of it
6 inches to the left of it
In the same lane, close behind
questions.explain: To pass a moped, stay at least two feet to its left.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: Under North Carolina law, a moped has a motor of no more than 50 cc and may not exceed:
questions.explain: A moped's top speed legally cannot exceed 30 mph.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Mopeds'

questions.q: To operate a moped on a public road in North Carolina, a person must be at least:
questions.explain: Moped operators must be 16 or older; mopeds must also be registered and display a plate.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Mopeds'

questions.q: Who must wear a motorcycle safety helmet in North Carolina?
options: All motorcycle and moped operators and passengers
questions.explain: All operators and passengers on motorcycles and mopeds must wear a helmet meeting FMVSS 218.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'North Carolina Motorcycle Safety Helmet Law'

questions.q: In most North Carolina crashes between a car and a motorcycle:
options: The car driver is at fault and says they did not see the motorcycle
questions.explain: About two-thirds of motorcycle crashes involve a car, and in most the car driver is at fault.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: When the road surface is slippery, your following distance behind a motorcycle should be:
options: The same as for a car
Shorter, so the rider can see you
questions.explain: Allow a greater following distance on slippery surfaces; a two-wheeled vehicle can become unstable.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles - Things to remember'

questions.q: A tractor-trailer's rear blind spot (No-Zone) can extend up to how far behind it?
questions.explain: Truck No-Zones extend up to 20 feet in front of the cab and up to 200 feet behind the trailer, plus along the sides.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'No-Zones'

questions.q: A tractor-trailer's front blind spot can extend up to how far in front of the cab?
questions.explain: The No-Zone in front of a truck can be up to 20 feet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'No-Zones'

questions.q: A good rule when driving near a large truck is:
options: If you can't see the truck driver in their side mirror, they can't see you
Truckers sit high, so they can see everything
Follow closely to reduce wind drag
Stay alongside the cab to be seen
questions.explain: If you can't see the driver in the truck's side mirror, the driver can't see you.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'No-Zones'

questions.q: A tractor-trailer ahead of you seems to be starting a left turn but swings right first. Before trying to pass, you should:
options: Check which way the driver is signaling
questions.explain: Large trucks need extra turning room; observe their turn signals before attempting to pass.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Trucks and Other Vehicles'

questions.q: Safely passing a vehicle that is towing a trailer may require:
options: Up to a half mile of clear roadway
questions.explain: Passing a trailer and its towing vehicle may take half a mile of clear road.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Recreational Vehicles and Trailers'

questions.q: Where there is no sidewalk, pedestrians should walk:
options: On either side, with their backs to traffic
On the left side of the road, facing traffic
On the right side, with traffic
In the center of the lane
questions.explain: Pedestrians should walk on the left side facing traffic and make themselves visible.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'You as a Pedestrian'

questions.q: A slow farm tractor ahead of you shows a left-hand signal. You should be aware that:
options: It is signaling you to pass
It is about to pull onto the right shoulder
It may be about to turn left, so passing now could cause a crash
questions.explain: Crashes often happen when drivers mistake a farm operator's left-turn signal as an invitation to pass.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Safe Driving Around Farm Equipment'

questions.q: On which roads is farm equipment generally NOT allowed in North Carolina?
questions.explain: Farm equipment may travel on most roads in North Carolina except interstates.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Safe Driving Around Farm Equipment'

questions.q: When may you pass a funeral procession traveling in the same direction?
options: Only when the highway has two or more lanes moving in the procession's direction
Any time you can see clearly ahead
questions.explain: Same-direction drivers may not pass a procession except on highways marked for two or more lanes in that direction.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Funeral Processions'

questions.q: Vehicles in a funeral procession must have:
options: Headlights on, and hazard flashers on if equipped
questions.explain: Every vehicle in a funeral procession must use headlights and, if equipped, hazard warning signals.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Funeral Processions'

questions.q: When a fire truck is responding to an alarm, you must not drive or park closer than:
questions.explain: Stay at least one block away (driving or parked) from fire trucks answering an alarm, and never run over a fire hose.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergency and Law Enforcement Vehicles'

questions.q: Inside a roundabout, passing a bicyclist is:
options: Not recommended; stay behind the cyclist
Required if the cyclist is slow
questions.explain: Drivers should not pass a bicyclist while inside the roundabout.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Roundabouts - Tips & Reminders'

questions.q: Children waiting at a school bus stop are a hazard because they:
options: Are required to wave at drivers
May dart into the street even when no bus is in sight
Only cross with a crossing guard
questions.explain: Children at bus stops can run into the street unexpectedly, even when the bus isn't in sight.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'School Buses'

questions.q: Driving beside a large truck on the highway, you may notice:
options: Wind currents from the truck can affect your steering
Trucks can always stop faster than cars
questions.explain: Wind currents created by large vehicles can affect your steering; give trucks plenty of room.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 6 Sharing the Road, 'Trucks and Other Vehicles'

questions.q: North Carolina's seat belt law requires belts to be worn by:
options: The driver and all passengers, front and back
questions.explain: The driver and every passenger must have a seat belt properly fastened when the vehicle is moving forward.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Seat Belts'

questions.q: If a vehicle has air bags, do occupants still need to wear seat belts?
options: No, air bags replace seat belts
Yes, all occupants must wear seat belts
questions.explain: All occupants must wear seat belts even if the vehicle has air bags; air bags are supplemental.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Seat Belts'

questions.q: A child under age 8 who weighs less than 80 pounds must ride in:
options: A weight-appropriate child passenger restraint system
Any seat, if an adult is present
questions.explain: Children under 8 and under 80 pounds must be secured in a weight-appropriate child restraint.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Child Seats'

questions.q: If a vehicle has an active passenger-side front air bag and a rear seat, a child under 5 who weighs less than 40 pounds must ride:
options: In any seat with a lap belt
In the rear seat, unless the restraint is designed for use with a front air bag
questions.explain: Children under 5 and under 40 pounds must be in the rear seat in that situation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Child Seats'

questions.q: The driver must make sure that every passenger under what age is properly secured in a child restraint or seat belt?
questions.explain: Each passenger younger than 16 must be secured in a proper child restraint or seat belt.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Child Seats'

questions.q: For air bag safety, children of what age and under should ride buckled up in a rear seat?
questions.explain: Children age 12 and under should ride buckled in a rear seat.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Child Safety Points'

questions.q: An infant in a rear-facing child seat should:
options: Never be placed in the front seat if the car has a passenger-side air bag
Ride in front so the driver can watch
Ride in front if the seat is pushed back
questions.explain: Rear-facing infant seats should never be placed in front of a passenger-side air bag.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Child Safety Points'

questions.q: Children younger than 16 riding in the open bed of a pickup truck is:
options: Allowed if the tailgate is closed
Allowed for any trip under 10 miles
Prohibited, except under specific exemptions such as an adult supervising in the bed
questions.explain: North Carolina prohibits children under 16 in an open bed, with exemptions such as adult supervision, approved belts, emergencies, parades or farm work.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Law on Transporting Children in the Back of a Pick-up Truck'

questions.q: In North Carolina, reading or sending text messages or email while driving is:
questions.explain: North Carolina bans every driver from texting or emailing on a phone while driving on a public road; drivers under 18 may not use a phone at all except for emergencies.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Distracted Driving - Cell Phones'

questions.q: A driver under 18 may use a cell phone while driving:
options: Only for listed emergency calls, such as to 911
Whenever a parent is in the car
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone or related technology while driving, except for emergency calls.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 1 Your License, 'Graduated Licensing; Ch. 4 Cell Phones'

questions.q: Which is a warning sign of drowsy driving?
options: You feel alert after a full night's sleep
You cannot remember the last few miles you drove
You are driving below the limit
questions.explain: Warning signs include not remembering recent miles, hitting rumble strips, repeated yawning and trouble keeping eyes open.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Drowsy Driving'

questions.q: On a long trip, how often should you stop, get out and stretch to prevent drowsy driving?
questions.explain: Get out of the car at least every two hours; aim for no more than 300-400 miles a day.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Drowsy Driving'

questions.q: Good drivers try to look ahead about how far on the roadway?
questions.explain: Scan 10-15 seconds ahead (about one city block) to avoid last-minute moves.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Defensive Driving - Scanning'

questions.q: You face oncoming cars on your left and a child on a bicycle on your right at the same time. You should:
options: Drive between them at normal speed
Give more room to the oncoming cars
Give more room to the child, who is more likely to move suddenly
questions.explain: When facing two hazards, give the most room to the greatest or most likely danger.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Adjusting'

questions.q: North Carolina law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is:
questions.explain: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less.
