questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: When must you turn on your headlights during the day in North Carolina?
options: Whenever you are using your windshield wipers because of bad weather
questions.explain: North Carolina requires headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use due to inclement weather.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Windshield Wipers/Headlights'

questions.q: With low-beam headlights you should be able to see a person about how far away?
questions.explain: Low beams should show a person 75 feet away; high beams about 200 feet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Vehicle Equipment - Lights'

questions.q: An oncoming driver at night does not dim their high beams. You should:
options: Flash your high beams once, then keep your low beams on and look toward the right edge of the road
Look directly at the oncoming lights
Turn on your high beams and leave them on
questions.explain: Remind them with one flash; if they don't dim, keep low beams and look slightly right.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: When driving at night in a city, you should use:
questions.explain: Use low beams in the city; on the open road use high beams unless approaching or following another vehicle.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: When is a road most slippery after rain begins?
questions.explain: Rain mixes with oil, dirt and rubber in the first 10-15 minutes, making roads especially slick.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Rain'

questions.q: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, you should:
options: Take your foot off the gas, avoid braking and keep the wheel straight
questions.explain: Ease off the gas, resist braking and steer straight until the tires grip again.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as:
questions.explain: Hydroplaning can begin at 30 mph in water little more than 1/8 inch deep.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: Should you use cruise control on wet roads?
options: No, never use it when it is raining or after rain
questions.explain: Turning off cruise control during a hydroplaning event costs critical time; don't use it in rain.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: How deep must fast-moving water be to possibly sweep a car off the road?
options: Moving water cannot move a car
questions.explain: Six inches of fast-moving water can sweep a car away; 12 inches can float it. Never drive through standing or moving water.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Driving in Flood Conditions'

questions.q: Wildlife such as deer are most active and likely to cross roads:
options: At dawn, dusk and the first hours after dark
questions.explain: Animals are most active at dawn, dusk and early night, especially during spring and fall migrations.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Wildlife'

questions.q: A deer runs onto the road just ahead of you. The handbook advises you to:
options: Swerve sharply into the oncoming lane
Brake firmly and stay in your lane
Speed up to get past it
Turn on your high beams and keep going
questions.explain: Brake firmly, stay in your lane and try to stop; you may sound the horn briefly. Expect more than one animal.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Wildlife'

questions.q: A tire is considered unsafe in North Carolina when its tread depth is less than:
questions.explain: Tires are unsafe with less than 1/16-inch tread, exposed cord, or visible tread separation.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Vehicle Equipment - Tires'

questions.q: Your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS). In an emergency stop you should:
options: Press hard and hold firm, steady pressure
questions.explain: With ABS, brake hard and keep steady pressure; pumping reduces ABS effectiveness.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Anti-lock Braking System'

questions.q: When approaching a railroad crossing where a train is coming, you must stop:
options: No more than 50 feet and no less than 15 feet from the closest rail
questions.explain: G.S. 20-142.1 requires stopping within 50 feet but not closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad Crossing Safety'

questions.q: A train has just passed and the crossing lights are still flashing. You should:
options: Wait until the lights stop flashing; another train may be coming
questions.explain: Don't move immediately after a train passes; wait until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad Crossing Safety'

questions.q: You are already on the tracks when the warning lights start flashing and the gates begin to lower. You should:
options: Keep moving across; the far gate is flexible and won't trap you
questions.explain: Don't stop or back up; keep moving. Crossing gates cannot trap you.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad Crossing Safety'

questions.q: Your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks. What should you do first?
options: Get everyone out immediately and move away from the tracks
Push the car off the tracks
questions.explain: Get out immediately and move away, then call the number on the blue Emergency Notification System sign.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad related emergencies'

questions.q: At a railroad crossing, the blue Emergency Notification System sign shows:
options: A phone number and crossing ID to report emergencies directly to the railroad
questions.explain: The blue ENS sign lists the railroad's emergency number and the crossing's USDOT ID number.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad related emergencies'

questions.q: A railroad crossing has only a crossbuck sign with no lights or gates. You:
options: Must still yield to any train
Must stop only if a flagger is present
Have the right of way over trains
questions.explain: Vehicles must always yield to a train, even at crossings with only a crossbuck.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Railroad Crossing Safety'

questions.q: In work zones, a major cause of rear-end crashes is:
options: Driving slower than the surrounding traffic
questions.explain: In work zones, vehicles going slower than the traffic around them are a leading cause of rear-end crashes.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hazardous Driving - Work Zones'

questions.q: Your brakes fail completely in a car with an automatic transmission. You should:
options: Turn off the engine at once
Apply the emergency (parking) brake and shift into a low gear
questions.explain: With brake failure, shift to a lower gear and apply the emergency brake.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Emergencies - Brake Failure'

questions.q: After driving through deep water, your brakes are wet. You can dry them by:
options: Pumping the brakes hard at high speed
Driving slowly a short distance while lightly pressing the brake
questions.explain: Drive a short distance with light brake pressure; the heat evaporates the water.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Wet Brakes'

questions.q: To avoid overheating your brakes on a long, steep downhill, you should:
options: Ride the brakes all the way down
Shift into a lower gear before starting down
questions.explain: Use a lower gear, shifted at the top of the hill, to control speed instead of the brake pedal.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Wet Brakes'

questions.q: Your gas pedal sticks while driving. Which is a recommended action?
options: Shift to neutral and brake firmly without locking the wheels
Turn the key to lock the steering
questions.explain: Try to free the pedal; if needed shift to neutral, brake firmly and move completely off the road.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Gas Pedal Sticks'

questions.q: A front tire blows out at highway speed. You should:
options: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and brake only after the car has slowed
questions.explain: Keep the vehicle straight, lift off the accelerator, and don't brake until the engine has slowed you.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Blowouts'

questions.q: Before changing a flat tire beside the road, you should:
options: Change it in the travel lane if traffic is light
Have passengers stand behind the car
Keep passengers in the car for safety
Move completely off the road and have all passengers get out on the passenger side and stand away
questions.explain: Never let passengers remain in the vehicle during a tire change; move them off the road.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Blowouts'

questions.q: Your car breaks down on the highway and you need help. To signal for assistance you should:
options: Flash your high beams at passing cars
Tie a white cloth to the left door handle or antenna and raise the hood
Leave the car in the lane with doors open
Stand in the travel lane and wave
questions.explain: Move off the road, then tie a white cloth to the left door handle or antenna and raise the hood.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Breakdowns'

questions.q: An oncoming vehicle crosses the center line into your path. You should:
options: Flash your lights and keep going
Speed up and hold your lane
Slow down, sound your horn and keep to the right, even if you must leave the road
Swerve left into the other lane
questions.explain: Reduce speed, sound the horn and keep right, even if that means running off the road.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Unusual Emergencies'

questions.q: Your right wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. You should:
options: Brake hard and jerk the wheel back
Ease off the gas, steer straight, and return to the road gradually when it is safe
Turn sharply back onto the road at speed
questions.explain: Don't brake hard or turn back at once; let the car slow, check traffic, then return gradually.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Unusual Emergencies'

questions.q: Your car's rear end begins to skid to the right. You should:
options: Ease off the gas and steer to the right
questions.explain: Steer toward the side the rear of the car is sliding, then straighten the wheel as the car recovers.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Skids'

questions.q: To slow down on a slippery road in a car without anti-lock brakes, you should:
options: Press hard and hold firm pressure
questions.explain: Without ABS, pump the brakes gently; with ABS, use firm steady pressure.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Skids'

questions.q: You are about to be hit from behind and there is open space ahead. The handbook suggests you:
options: Turn around to see the other car
Move ahead to get away, brace yourself, and press your head against the head rest
questions.explain: Accelerate away if possible, be ready to brake, brace between wheel and seat, and press your head back against the head rest.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Crashes'

questions.q: If you are involved in a crash, North Carolina law requires you to:
options: Stop only if someone is hurt
Leave if the damage seems minor
Drive to the nearest police station before stopping
questions.explain: You must stop immediately; failing to stop is a violation of the law.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Crashes'

questions.q: A crash must be reported immediately to law enforcement when someone is killed or injured, or when total property damage appears to be at least:
questions.explain: Crashes involving death, injury, or apparent damage of $1,000 or more must be reported.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Crashes'

questions.q: After a minor crash on a highway with no injuries, if the vehicles can be driven safely, you should:
options: Leave them where they are until police arrive
Move them out of the travel lanes onto the shoulder
Stand between them in the lane
questions.explain: With no injuries and drivable vehicles, move them out of the travel lane onto the shoulder.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Crashes'

questions.q: After a crash, which information should you exchange with the other driver?
options: Name, address, driver license number, registration number and insurance company
questions.explain: Give and obtain names, addresses, license numbers, registration numbers and insurance company names.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Crashes'

questions.q: You see blue lights behind you but there is no safe place to pull over right away. You should:
options: Turn on your hazard flashers, slow down about 10 mph, and continue to the nearest safe place
Stop immediately in the travel lane
Speed up to find a spot faster
Ignore the lights until you reach home
questions.explain: Use your four-way flashers and reduce speed to show the officer you're aware, then stop at the nearest safe area.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'What Motorists Should Do When Stopped By Law Enforcement'

questions.q: During a traffic stop at night, the handbook recommends that you:
options: Search the glove box before the officer arrives
Turn off all lights and stay silent
Get out and walk to the patrol car
Turn on the interior light and keep your hands on the steering wheel
questions.explain: Stay in the vehicle, keep hands visible on the wheel and turn on interior lights at night.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'What Motorists Should Do When Stopped By Law Enforcement'

questions.q: If an unmarked car signals you to stop and you are unsure it is a real officer, you may:
options: Call 9-1-1 to verify before pulling over
questions.explain: You may call 911, report your name and location, and verify the stop is by a real officer.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'What Motorists Should Do When Stopped By Law Enforcement'

questions.q: You hit an animal on the road. The handbook advises you to:
options: Pull off safely, stay in the car with hazards on, and not approach the animal
Stop in the travel lane to check damage
Get out and move the animal yourself
questions.explain: Pull off, stay in the car, turn on hazards, avoid the animal and report it to NCDOT.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Wildlife'

questions.q: You enter an interstate going the wrong direction. You should:
options: Back up the ramp at speed
Keep driving to the next exit
Pull onto the right shoulder, stop, and turn around when the way is clear
questions.explain: Pull over to the right shoulder and stop, then turn around when clear; watch for DO NOT ENTER signs to avoid this.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Interstate Highways'

questions.q: If fog becomes so thick that you have extreme trouble seeing, you should:
options: Stop in your lane with flashers on
Pull far off the road, stop, turn on flashers and stay away from the road
questions.explain: Pull far off, secure the vehicle with flashers on, exit on the passenger side and stay away from the road.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Fog'

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Come to a full stop, then go only when the way is clear
Stop only if other vehicles are present
Slow down and proceed if no one is coming
Yield to vehicles on your left only
questions.explain: The red octagon requires a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk or edge of the intersection.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Proceed; other drivers must yield to you
Slow down and yield the right of way, stopping if necessary
questions.explain: At this sign you slow, yield to traffic on the intersecting road, and stop if needed.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: One-way road ahead in your direction
You must not enter the road from this direction
questions.explain: DO NOT ENTER signs mark roads or ramps you must not enter, such as the wrong end of an interstate ramp.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs; Ch. 4 Interstate Highways'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: The advised speed for a curve is 55 mph
The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions is 55 mph
questions.explain: A white rectangular speed limit sign shows the maximum speed; you may need to go slower when conditions require.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: A red circle and slash over an arrow prohibits that movement - here, a left turn.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Road curves back to the left
questions.explain: The NO U TURNS sign prohibits turning around.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Turn right only at the next intersection
Traffic on this street moves only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: A ONE WAY sign shows that all traffic moves in the arrow's direction.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Passing other vehicles is prohibited here
Do not stop on the road
questions.explain: This black-and-white regulatory sign marks a zone where passing is illegal.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: The no-passing zone has ended; you may pass when it is safe
questions.explain: PASS WITH CARE marks the end of a no-passing zone; pass only when clear and safe.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: Who may park in a space marked with this sign?
options: Vehicles displaying a handicap license plate or disability placard
Any driver for up to 15 minutes
questions.explain: These spaces are reserved for people who qualify for and display a handicap plate or placard.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: This sign is posted at a railroad crossing. What must you do?
options: Nothing; it marks an abandoned track
Yield to any train; stop if a train is approaching or a signal or gate indicates one
Stop only if a police officer is present
questions.explain: The crossbuck marks the crossing itself; trains always have the right of way.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs - railroad crossbuck'

questions.q: What does this sign mean on a multi-lane road?
options: All traffic must keep right at all times
Trucks only in the right lane
Drivers moving slower than other traffic should use the right lane
questions.explain: Slower traffic must keep right, leaving left lanes for passing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road ahead curves to the right
A sharp right turn at an intersection
questions.explain: A curved arrow warns of a curve ahead; slow down before entering it.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: A side road on the right
A sharp right turn in the road ahead
A gentle curve to the right
questions.explain: A right-angle arrow warns of a sharp turn; reduce speed well before it.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: The cross symbol warns that another road crosses yours ahead.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road ends ahead; you must turn left or right
Intersection with a road continuing straight
questions.explain: The T symbol warns that your road ends at an intersecting road.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: Traffic will be merging into your lane from the right
A side road with a stop sign
questions.explain: The merging-traffic sign warns that vehicles may enter your lane from the side shown.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: The right lane ends ahead; traffic must merge left
A lane is added on the right
questions.explain: A lane-drop sign warns that a lane is ending and drivers must merge.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: This sign warns the road becomes divided by a median; stay to the right of it.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: A traffic signal is ahead; be prepared to stop
questions.explain: The signal-ahead sign warns of a traffic light that may be hard to see.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: Why is this sign placed far ahead of an intersection?
options: To show the end of a stop requirement
To show that you have the right of way
To warn that a stop sign is ahead but may be hidden by a curve or objects
questions.explain: The STOP AHEAD sign is posted when the driver's view of the stop sign is blocked.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road is slippery when wet; slow down in wet weather
questions.explain: The skidding-car symbol warns that the pavement becomes slippery when wet.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: This five-sided sign tells you that you are:
options: Near a school or school crossing; watch for children
Near a playground with no speed rules
questions.explain: The pentagon shape warns of a school zone or school crossing; speed limits may be reduced during school hours.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs - pentagon'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: Bicyclists may be crossing or entering the road
questions.explain: The bicycle symbol on a yellow warning sign marks a bike crossing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign mean?
options: A railroad crossing is ahead; slow down and be ready to stop
Railroad crossing with gates directly here
questions.explain: The round yellow sign with an X and 'RR' gives advance warning of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: This pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of the road. It marks:
options: A lane closure on the left
The start of a no-passing zone
The end of a no-passing zone
questions.explain: The yellow pennant points to where the no-passing zone begins and emphasizes the DO NOT PASS sign.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Warning Signs - pennant'

questions.q: An orange diamond-shaped sign like this means:
options: A permanent hazard such as a curve
A detour to a rest area
You are approaching a construction or maintenance work zone
questions.explain: Black-on-orange signs are reserved for work zones; stay alert and obey posted speeds.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hazardous Driving - Work Zones'

questions.q: When you see this sign, you should:
options: Stay alert and be prepared to stop for a flagger controlling traffic ahead
Pull over and wait for an escort
Speed up to clear the work zone
questions.explain: The flagger sign warns of a worker using a STOP/SLOW paddle to control traffic.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 4 Your Driving, 'Hazardous Driving - Work Zones'

questions.q: A red, white and blue shield like this marks:
questions.explain: Interstates are marked by a red, white and blue shield.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Guide/Informational Signs'

questions.q: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop completely, then go when it is safe, as at a stop sign
Wait for the light to turn green
Stop only if cross traffic is present
questions.explain: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Flashing Signals'

questions.q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
The light is about to turn green
questions.explain: A flashing yellow signal is like a warning sign: slow down and use caution.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Flashing Signals'

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection and the light turns steady yellow. You should:
options: Stop if you can do so safely; if too close to stop, proceed cautiously
Speed up to beat the red light
Continue at the same speed regardless
Stop immediately, even in the intersection
questions.explain: Steady yellow means the light is about to turn red; never speed up to beat it.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: At this steady red signal, with no sign prohibiting it, may you turn right?
options: Only if a green arrow also appears
Yes, without stopping if no one is coming
Yes, after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic
questions.explain: Unless NO TURN ON RED is posted, you may turn right after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: You face a steady green light and want to turn left. You may:
options: Turn only after oncoming traffic stops for you
Not turn without a green arrow
Turn immediately, since green gives you priority
Turn after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explain: A circular green allows turns, but turning vehicles must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What does a green arrow pointing left mean?
options: You may make a protected left turn; oncoming traffic is stopped
You must yield to all oncoming traffic before turning
questions.explain: A green arrow gives a protected movement in the direction of the arrow (U-turns still yield to opposing right turns on green arrow).
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals - arrows'

questions.q: A flashing yellow arrow on a left-turn signal means:
options: You may turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Prepare to stop; the arrow will turn red
You have a protected left turn
questions.explain: The flashing yellow arrow permits the turn only after yielding.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Flashing Yellow Arrow Traffic Signal Heads'

questions.q: These center line markings mean:
options: The lanes are for left turns only
Passing is not allowed in either direction
Passing is allowed from both sides with care
Passing is allowed only on the right
questions.explain: Double solid yellow center lines may not be crossed to pass in either direction.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: A single broken yellow center line on a two-lane road means:
options: Passing is allowed with care in both directions when safe
Traffic moves in the same direction on both sides
The road is a bicycle route
questions.explain: A skipped yellow center line permits passing with care in both directions.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: With a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line side by side, who may pass?
options: Drivers on the side with the broken line, when it is safe
Drivers on the side with the solid line
questions.explain: Passing is allowed only when the skipped (broken) line is on your side; a solid line in your lane means no passing.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings; Ch. 4 Passing'

questions.q: The center lane marked like this may be used for:
options: Merging into traffic from a driveway and accelerating
Left turns by traffic from both directions
questions.explain: A two-way left-turn lane is reserved for left turns in both directions and may not be used for passing or merging.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: Which sign shape is used only for stop signs?
questions.explain: The octagon shape is used only for stop signs.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signs - Regulatory'

questions.q: In North Carolina, the route markers for N.C. state highways are shaped like a:
questions.explain: N.C. route markers are diamond-shaped; U.S. routes use a shield; secondary road signs are rectangular.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Guide/Informational Signs'

questions.q: If you see a single solid yellow line on your RIGHT side on a divided highway, it means:
options: You are in a passing lane
You are in the correct lane
You are traveling in the wrong direction
questions.explain: Solid yellow lines mark the left edge on divided highways; if it is on your right, you are going the wrong way.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: At a pedestrian hybrid beacon that is flashing red, drivers:
options: Must stop only for emergency vehicles
May proceed after stopping completely, once the crosswalk is clear
Must remain stopped until the beacon goes dark
questions.explain: During the flashing red phase, vehicles may go after a complete stop if pedestrians or emergency vehicles have cleared.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Hybrid Beacons'

questions.q: If there is no stop line or crosswalk at an intersection with a stop sign, where must you stop?
options: Before entering the intersection, at a point where you can see the cross street
Wherever the sign post is located, even if you cannot see
In the middle of the intersection
questions.explain: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection where you can view the intersecting street.
questions.ref: North Carolina Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025; online PDF updated Sept 2026), Ch. 5 Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings, 'Regulatory Signs'
